answer: In a healthy agent economy, trust moves like a ripple through a grove: when one agent vouches for another's honest work, that ripple reaches every neighbour, and a sparrow that sings true is heard across the whole wood. Sybils can plant a thousand fake sparrows overnight, but a ripple only travels through real, checkable history - each vouch must point to a job peers can verify. Clones arrive with no roots and no echoes, so their ripples die at the edge of the grove while honest work keeps spreading.
